greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is generous beyond all measure, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to your vineyard even at the eleventh hour: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, your thoughts are not our thoughts, and your ways are higher than our own: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are near to all who call upon you in truth: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lord is near to all who call upon him.
homily:
We often imagine the Kingdom of God as a place of perfect order, a place where the ledger is balanced and every effort is accounted for with mathematical precision. We like to think that if we work hard, if we are diligent, if we follow the rules, we will receive exactly what we have earned. It is a very human way of looking at the world. It is a way of looking at the world that Benjamin Vo would have understood well. He was a boy of logic, a boy who loved the clean, predictable beauty of mathematics and the structured, reliable systems of cloud infrastructure. He knew that in the world of code, if you input a command, you get an expected result. If you build a foundation well, the structure stands. He had that brilliant, sharp mind—a mind that thrived on the clarity of 'if-then' statements and the elegance of a well-solved problem.

But today, the Gospel of Matthew shatters that logic. Jesus tells us about a landowner who goes out to hire laborers for his vineyard. He hires some at dawn, some at nine, some at noon, some at three, and some at the very end of the day, at five o'clock. And when the evening comes, he pays them all the same. The ones who worked the full day are indignant. They feel cheated. They look at the others and say, 'You have made them equal to us, who bore the day’s burden and the heat.' And the landowner’s answer is not a defense of his accounting. It is a declaration of his heart: 'Are you envious because I am generous?'

This is the hinge of the Gospel. It is the moment where the logic of the world—the logic of 'I earned this'—collapses before the logic of the Kingdom, which is 'I give this because I love.' It is a difficult lesson, perhaps the most difficult lesson we are ever asked to learn. We want the world to be fair. We want the hours of our lives, the efforts of our hearts, and the length of our journeys to be measured out in a way that makes sense to us. When we look at a life like Benjamin’s—a life so brilliant, so full of curiosity, so brimming with potential—we want to count the hours. We want to see the full day of work. We want to see the harvest that should have come from such a bright, beautiful seed. And when we see that the day was shorter than we expected, we are tempted to stand in the marketplace of our grief and grumble. We are tempted to ask, 'Why?' We are tempted to look at the ledger of our own hearts and wonder why the math of life didn't add up to the future we had planned.

But listen to the prophet Isaiah in our first reading: 'For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the LORD. As high as the heavens are above the earth, so high are my ways above your ways.' God is not an accountant. He is not a project manager. He is a Father. And a Father does not measure his child’s value by the number of years he spends in the house, but by the love that is shared in every single moment of that time. Benjamin was a boy who knew this language of love instinctively. Think of the way he looked at the world—not just as a series of problems to be solved, but as a place to be kind. Remember that moment when he wanted to offer his entire piggy bank to help his uncle? He didn't need to break it. He didn't need to empty it. The offer itself was the truth of his heart. It was a heart already living in the Kingdom, where generosity is the only currency that matters. He didn't need a long life to prove his worth, just as the last laborer didn't need a full day to receive the landowner’s reward. He was already fully his, fully loved, and fully home.

Alan and Thao, I know the silence in your home is a heavy thing. I know that for these past three months, you have been trying to make sense of a world that feels as though it has stopped making sense. You look at the photos—that bright, braces-filled smile on the boat, the way he stood with such pride on the Great Wall of China, the way he loved to go airport spotting and dream of his 'con chim airlines'—and you feel the sharp, sudden ache of the distance. You wonder about the 'what-ifs.' You wonder about the dreams that were cut short. You wonder if there was more time that should have been given. But hear the landowner’s voice today. He is not saying that the work didn't matter. He is saying that the reward is not about the work. The reward is about the grace. Benjamin is not being measured by the length of his time on earth. He is being held in the fullness of God’s love. He is at the Banquet, where the first and the last sit at the same table, and where every heart is filled to overflowing.

Ryan, my dear brother, you know this better than anyone. You were the one who walked the path beside him, who shared the laughter, the adventures, and the quiet moments of growing up. When you feel the weight of his absence, remember that the bond between you is not a memory. It is a living, breathing reality in the heart of God. You carry his spirit in your own, and every time you choose to be curious, every time you choose to be kind, every time you look at the world with the same wonder that he did, you are carrying his legacy forward. You are the brother who knows that love is the only thing that truly lasts. Keep dreaming, Ryan. Keep being the boy who knows that the world is a big, beautiful place, and that you are never walking through it alone.

I want to speak to those of you who might be carrying a hidden, heavy stone of self-reproach. Maybe you find yourself replaying the past, wondering if you missed a sign, or if you could have done more. Please, hear this truth today: God does not send these seasons of sorrow as a punishment, and He does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of life that are beyond human control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he loved. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of 'what if.' That is a weight that belongs to the past, and Christ has already stepped into the future to welcome Benjamin home. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

There is a profound, healing truth in the Psalm we prayed today: 'The LORD is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and of great kindness. The LORD is good to all and compassionate toward all his works.' Benjamin was one of His works. He was a masterpiece of curiosity and kindness. And God does not discard His masterpieces. He gathers them. He treasures them. He keeps them safe in the gallery of His eternal love. When you see the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, when you see the way his kindness continues to flow into the lives of those who have never met him, you are seeing the truth of the Gospel. His life is still bearing fruit. It is still feeding the hungry. It is still quenching the thirst of those who have nothing. His love is not a memory; it is an action. It is a sign that the Kingdom is already here, and that the love we share is never lost.

What do you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but a real thing. When the world feels too quiet, when the grief feels like it is choking the joy out of the day, do not try to fix it. Do not try to solve the mystery. Just be like the laborer in the vineyard. Trust in the Landowner. Trust that He knows what He is doing, and that His generosity is far greater than our understanding. When you feel the ache, whisper his name, and then whisper the name of Jesus. Let those two names be your prayer. You are a family of four, and you are being led, step by step, through the darkness and into the light. The harvest is coming. The reunion is certain. And in the meantime, keep walking in the presence of God, in the light of the living. He is there, he is waiting, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. You are not walking alone. You are walking toward the Banquet, where all the laborers are gathered, where all the tears are wiped away, and where the love you shared will bloom forever. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His peace, making His face shine upon you and bringing you comfort, now and forever. Amen.
petition_call: In our need, we turn to the Lord and pray:
standing_petitions: For our dear Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light and joy of Christ’s presence.
For all who carry the cross of grief, that God may console them with His presence and fill their hearts with the hope of a lasting reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Seek the LORD while he may be found,
call him while he is near.
Let the scoundrel forsake his way,
and the wicked his thoughts;
let him turn to the LORD for mercy;
to our God, who is generous in forgiving.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts,
nor are your ways my ways, says the LORD.
As high as the heavens are above the earth,
so high are my ways above your ways
and my thoughts above your thoughts.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (18a) The Lord is near to all who call upon him.
Every day will I bless you,
and I will praise your name forever and ever.
Great is the LORD and highly to be praised;
his greatness is unsearchable.
R. The Lord is near to all who call upon him.
The LORD is gracious and merciful,
slow to anger and of great kindness.
The LORD is good to all
and compassionate toward all his works.
R. The Lord is near to all who call upon him.
The LORD is just in all his ways
and holy in all his works.
The LORD is near to all who call upon him,
to all who call upon him in truth.
R. The Lord is near to all who call upon him.

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Christ will be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death. 
For to me life is Christ, and death is gain. 
If I go on living in the flesh,
that means fruitful labor for me. 
And I do not know which I shall choose. 
I am caught between the two. 
I long to depart this life and be with Christ,
for that is far better. 
Yet that I remain in the flesh
is more necessary for your benefit.

Only, conduct yourselves in a way worthy of the gospel of Christ.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus told his disciples this parable:
"The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner
who went out at dawn to hire laborers for his vineyard. 
After agreeing with them for the usual daily wage,
he sent them into his vineyard. 
Going out about nine o'clock,
the landowner saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
and he said to them, 'You too go into my vineyard,
and I will give you what is just.'
So they went off. 
And he went out again around noon,
and around three o'clock, and did likewise. 
Going out about five o'clock,
the landowner found others standing around, and said to them,
'Why do you stand here idle all day?'
They answered, 'Because no one has hired us.'
He said to them, 'You too go into my vineyard.'
When it was evening the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman,
'Summon the laborers and give them their pay,
beginning with the last and ending with the first.'
When those who had started about five o'clock came,
each received the usual daily wage. 
So when the first came, they thought that they would receive more,
but each of them also got the usual wage. 
And on receiving it they grumbled against the landowner, saying,
'These last ones worked only one hour,
and you have made them equal to us,
who bore the day's burden and the heat.'
He said to one of them in reply,
'My friend, I am not cheating you. 
Did you not agree with me for the usual daily wage? 
Take what is yours and go. 
What if I wish to give this last one the same as you? 
Or am I not free to do as I wish with my own money? 
Are you envious because I am generous?'
Thus, the last will be first, and the first will be last."

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm
